::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Shenzhen-state-backed memory venture founded March 2022 (registered capital ¥5 billion), led by CEO Liu Xiaoqiang (ex-TSMC fab manager) and initially by CSO Sakamoto Yukio (ex-Elpida CEO); the widely quoted '¥300 billion ambition / 140,000 wafers/month' plan is aspirational and unverified. Its 'novel memory production line project' (新型存储器产线) heads Shenzhen's 2025 major-industrial-project list, and 2025-2026 municipal water-use notices for wet-etch/CMP indicate process equipment is operating at plant level.
:::

**Chinese name:** 深圳市昇维旭技术有限公司 (Shēnzhèn Shì Shēngwéixù Jìshù Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

No verified product output yet; reported to target DRAM from 28nm-class nodes and new memory types.

## Why does it matter?

Added to the Entity List in the December 2, 2024 round; July 2026 reporting (via FT and reprints) describes it as one of the Huawei-linked 'Guanlan'-family Shenzhen sites and part of a government-SwaySure-Huawei triangle building 12-inch DRAM capacity — i.e., a key piece of China's most opaque memory push, with essentially no independently verified output.

## Project Timeline

- **Mar 2022** — Company founded, funded entirely by Shenzhen Industrial Investment Group
- **Dec 2024** — Added to the US Commerce Department's Entity List (SwaySure Technology Co., Ltd.)
- **Sep 2025** — Shenzhen lists its novel-memory line among top major industrial projects; process water permits confirm fab-level operations
- **Jul 2026** — Reports describe Huawei co-developing the 12-inch DRAM fab (140,000 wafers/month long-term plan, unverified)
